Exploration complete — all tasks done. Here's what I found about jinn's available plugins:

## Overview

`plugins/` contains **three first-party plugins**, all WASM guest payloads built against `jinn-plugin-api` (wire types) and `jinn-plugin-sdk` (`hello`/`push`/`welcome` helpers). Each declares a payload manifest in `[package.metadata.jinn]` with grants and an `http` flag. Two of them follow the same "scan → contribute → exit" pattern; one is stateful.

## The Plugins

**1. `persona-loader`** (353 lines)
- **Grants:** read-only `<config_dir>/personas`
- **What it does:** scans granted dirs for `*.md` persona files, parses `+++` TOML frontmatter (`name`, optional `description`) plus body, and pushes one `SetPersonaEntries` contribution. Earlier dirs shadow later ones (user-overrides-system). Bad files are skipped with a stderr note — one bad file never drops the batch.
- **Wire behavior:** `Hello` → `Welcome` → one `SetPersonaEntries` → exit.
- Also parses the shipped `res/personas/learning-tutor.md` in a test.

**2. `theme-loader`** (152 lines)
- **Grants:** read-only `<config_dir>/themes`
- **What it does:** scans for `*.toml` themes, reuses the **same loader core uses** (`jinn-theme::loader::discover_themes`), and translates each theme into `ThemeDef` — all ~41 color slots rendered as hex/ANSI strings — pushed as one `SetThemeEntries` contribution.
- **Wire behavior:** same one-shot pattern.

**3. `url-citations`** (470 + 695 lines) — the most sophisticated
- **Grants:** none — fully stateless (no filesystem/network); state lives only in memory
- **What it does:** **subscribes to host events** (`tool_call`, `tool_result`, `turn_end`) — the only plugin of the three that stays alive past handshake. It detects citable web sources by *shape*, not tool name:
  - **Call rule:** any http(s) URL in a tool call's JSON args becomes a pending candidate; promoted only if the result succeeds
  - **Result rule:** successful JSON results contribute every `{url|link, title}` object (handles doubly-encoded JSON strings like Z.ai's, bounded depth 8)
  - **Carve-out:** builtin `web-search` rebuilds the DuckDuckGo re-run URL from the query — the only tool-name-specific rule
- Citations buffer per-session, dedup by URL (later titled entry wins over empty title), and flush as one `PushCitations` on a **final-answer** turn end. Non-final turns retain the buffer; sessions are isolated.
- Code documents an ordering assumption: if citations ever land in the wrong turn's footer, the host's synchronous forwarding was violated.

## Key design takeaways

- **Contribution model:** plugins push data to the host via `PluginToHost` — currently `SetThemeEntries`, `SetPersonaEntries`, `PushCitations`. The host caches persona/theme sets even after the guest exits.
- **Grants system:** paths come only from the handshake `Welcome`; plugins never guess paths. `http = false` on all three today.
- **Guest laxity is deliberate:** plugins allow `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` — stdout/stderr *are* the wire; a dead guest just means no contribution.
- **Extending:** a new contribution type requires a new wire struct + `PluginToHost` variant (the codebase notes forgetting the enum variant is the most common oversight).

Want me to dig deeper into anything — e.g. the host side (`jinn-plugin` crate, how contributions land in AppState), the SDK handshake details, or the plugin authoring workflow (`jinn plugin add`)?

  8	### Subagents
  9	
 10	Subagents can be spawned using a new `task` tool and will appear in _purple text_ as a child session in the sidebar. The max depth is set to 1 prevent runaway cascading subagents.
 11	
 12	Subagent sessions are regular sessions that you can load to view their progress, steer, or cancel whenever desired. Once the subagent session returns to an IDLE state, the last message in the session (regardless of what it is) is sent back to the parent as a tool result. This makes it impossible to introduce a broken program state by manually working with a subagent since it's just a parent session calling a tool and waiting for the result.

Hand-authored values take precedence over API-discovered data and models.dev. Models that are only listed in `providers.toml` (never discovered) now appear in the model cache, so the status bar, compaction gate, and attachment gate resolve them; `input_modalities = ["text", "image"]` marks a local model vision-capable.
129	- Update learning-tutor persona.
130	- Skill preview rendering now uses a shared cache across all sessions.
131	- **Breaking:** `providers.toml` providers are now map-keyed tables (`[providers.<name>]`) instead of `[[providers]]` array-of-tables.
132	
133	### Map-Keyed Providers
134	
135	Nested tables are now part of the key path, so a nested table's provider is self-describing: `[providers.zai.extra_body]` and `[[providers.zai.model_info]]` unambiguously belong to zai instead of relying on which `[[providers]]` block came before them. Duplicate provider names are now rejected by TOML itself, and file order carries no meaning. Two things to know when converting an existing file: dotted names like `llama.cpp` are no longer valid as table keys (rename to something dot-free, e.g. `llamacpp`), and legacy files fail to load with an error naming the new syntax — the conversion is renaming each block header to `[providers.<its name>]` and deleting the `name =` key inside it.
136	
137	```toml
138	# example
139	[providers.llamacpp]
140	backend = "openai"
141	requires_key = false
142	base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8089/v1"
143	models = [
144	    "/path/to/model.gguf",
145	    "/foo/bar.gguf
146	]
147	
148	[[providers.llamacpp.model_info]]
149	id = "/path/to/model.gguf"
150	context_length = 96000
151	input_modalities = ["text", "image"]
152	
153	# the `bar.gguf` model is not listed, so it gets application defaults (unknown context + text-only modality)
154	```
155	
156	## 2026-08-07 v0.105.0
157	
158	- Add `F` keybind in Normal mode to create a _new_ session from an existing User or Assistant message _without_ existing history. Only the selected message will be present in the new session. The new session is not counted as a fork of the previous session since no history is preserved.
159	- Add `--dump-requests` debugging flag to get raw output of everything sent to a provider.
160	- Migrations should no longer fail if interrupted.
161	- Migrations performance improvement (single transaction).
162	
163	## 2026-08-03 v0.104.1
164	
165	- Simpler MCP configuration + added MCP configuration example
166	
167	## 2026-08-03 v0.104.0
168	
169	- MCP server sidebar entry only shows when MCP servers are enabled. Also uses consistent padding (1 cell top + 1 cell bottom).
170	- Uploaded tokens indicator now uses provider-returned value, falling back to local calculation.
171	- Cached tokens are now displayed (w/hexagon icon) next to uploaded tokens indicator as a percentage.
172	- Reasoning effort is now displayed upon starting `jinn`.
173	
174	### OpenRouter Provider Selection
175	
176	OpenRouter endpoints can now be selected using `<leader>sE` and selection is persisted per session. When using OpenRouter it's recommended to manually select a provider in order to maximize prompt cache pricing. Default behavior is unchanged and uses your OpenRouter account configuration for endpoints.
177	
178	## 2026-07-27 v0.103.0
179	
180	- `@` behavior now allows sending a message if the attachment cannot be found. Missing files are highlighted in red.
181	- `@` popup now scrolls.
182	
183	## 2026-07-25 v0.102.0
184	
185	- Fix slow startup performance on `install` and `config` commands.
186	- Add `--force` flag to `install` command to overwrite existing files.
187	- Fix positioning of file selection and prompt selection popups to be word-wrap aware. They now appear directly over the cursor instead of above the input box.
188	- Provide base directory in context for loaded skills to help agent load reference files.
189	- Add MCP server support.
190	- "Nag" system defaults changed: 200 chat entries + disabled
191	- Headed Chrome/Chromium instance restarts on connection lost. This happens if a `web_fetch` or `web_search` request hasn't happened for a while.
192	
193	## 2026-07-23 v0.101.0
194	
195	- Add ability to load skills directly via the skill picker using `<c-l>`.
196	- Skills that have been loaded can no longer be disabled from the skill picker.
197	
198	### New Feature: Project Record
199	
200	A new "record" file can be placed at `./agents/RECORD.md` which lists out current high-level facts about the project.
201	
202	The idea behind the record is that it always gets managed by a human and gets surfaced during every feature change. Humans can easily read and edit the record, and the agent has been instructed to only write approved edits to the record. The agent loads it and so gains an understanding of how things are _supposed_ to work which should (in theory) speed up codebase exploration during planning. It also helps (but doesn't eliminate) the problem of docs drifting from the actual implementation since the record gets referenced regularly.
203	
204	For example, a fact might be "The database backend is SQLite so the application can be ran easily standalone" and a new feature request might be "Add Postgres support". This pre-existing fact will get surfaced during planning so the developer can be made aware of potential implications of the feature.
205	
206	The implementation is prompt-based and all relevant planning and analysis prompts have been updated to support managing the record. Note that this takes slightly more tokens since extra work is being performed. But the token cost shouldn't be significant since the agent will already have the relevant code loaded into context during planning and evaluation.
207	
208	Currently its just a markdown file. As I experiment with using it, it might get changed to a vector search or some other lower-context mechanism.
209	
210	## 2026-07-21 v0.100.0
211	
212	- New "nag" system reminds agent to use the `todo_*` tools if they haven't done so after 100 chat entries.
213	- Add `cargo binstall` support
214	
215	## 2026-07-21 v0.97.0
216	
217	- Discord integration now allows selection of lifecycle script

# Jinn Changelog Report

**Scope:** 217 lines covering **24 releases** from v0.97.0 (2026-07-21) to v0.113.0 (unreleased). One breaking change noted. Three clear development themes dominate: **plugins**, **MCP**, and **session management**.

---

## 1. Unreleased (v0.113.0) — Subagents

The headline unreleased feature: a new `task` tool spawns subagent child sessions (purple in sidebar), **max depth 1** to prevent cascading. Subagents are ordinary sessions — loadable, steerable, cancellable — and when they return to IDLE their last message is sent back to the parent as the tool result, making it structurally impossible to corrupt state via manual subagent interaction. Also: `A` (archive session + children), `X` (teardown + archive children), unified confirmation wording.

## 2. Major Themes

### Plugin System (v0.107.0 → v0.110.0)
- **v0.107.0:** Experimental plugin system — Rust compiled to WASM.
- **v0.108.0:** `jinn install` now installs builtin plugins.
- **v0.110.0:** Citation tracking **moved out of core into a plugin**; new plugin status screen at `<leader>sP`.

### MCP Support (v0.102.0 → v0.110.0)
- **v0.102.0:** MCP server support lands; simplified config (v0.104.1).
- **v0.110.0:** Custom headers with `${ENV_VAR}` substitution; disabling an MCP server removes its tools from the session listing; `auto_enable` flag (MCP servers disabled by default).
- **v0.111.0:** Discord bot user filtering via `authorized_users` TOML list.

### Session Lifecycle & Context
- **v0.112.0:** `gci` keybind "isolates" a chat entry — motivated by the plan → isolate approved plan → implement with fresh context workflow. Also: context assembly order changed for the system prompt.
- **v0.105.0:** `F` creates a new session from a single message (not a fork — no history).
- **v0.109.0:** Tool calls grouped atomically — pins and context exclusion now operate on groups.

### Skills & Records
- **v0.101.0:** Project Record (`./agents/RECORD.md`) — human-managed high-level facts surfaced during planning, to speed exploration and fight doc drift. Prompt-based; may become vector search later.
- **v0.101.0/v0.106.0:** Skill picker `<c-l>` direct load; loaded skills can't be disabled; shared skill preview cache; base directory provided in skill context.

## 3. Breaking Change (v0.106.0)

`providers.toml` providers moved from `[[providers]]` array-of-tables to **map-keyed tables** (`[providers.<name>]`). Conversion: rename each header to `[providers.<its name>]`, delete the inner `name =` key. Gotchas: dotted names like `llama.cpp` are no longer valid keys; legacy files fail to load with an error naming the new syntax. Nested tables (e.g. `[[providers.zai.model_info]]`) are now unambiguously scoped, and TOML itself rejects duplicate provider names.

## 4. Provider & Model Handling

- **v0.106.0:** `[[providers.model_info]]` — per-model `context_length`, `input_modalities` (e.g. marking local models vision-capable), `extra_body` overrides. Hand-authored values beat API-discovered data; providers-only-in-toml now appear in the model cache.
- **v0.104.0:** OpenRouter endpoint selection (`<leader>sE`, persisted per session — recommended to maximize prompt-cache pricing); cached-token indicator (hexagon icon, percentage); provider-returned upload tokens.
- **v0.110.0:** Cache indicator colorized by hit rate (red <90%, yellow 90–94%, green 95%+).

## 5. Configuration Surface Growth

- **v0.110.0:** `disabled_tools` / `disabled_skills` (default posture: enable everything); everything applies to new sessions only.
- **v0.111.0:** `[discord]` block: `enabled`, `guild_id`, `forum_channel`, `authorized_users`. Minimal — no role filtering or allow-all.

## 6. Reliability & Fixes

| Version | Fix |
|---|---|
| v0.108.1–v0.108.3 | Tool/skill construction no longer busts cache; tools/skills moved to `BTreeMap` |
| v0.108.4 | Filters preventing invalid message sequencing reaching providers |
| v0.105.0 | Interrupted migrations no longer fail; single-transaction migration perf |
| v0.107.0 | Immediate exit on malformed `jinn.toml`/`providers.toml`; tool-output TUI leak fixed; yank returns full JSON (jq-friendly) |
| v0.112.1 | Windows: Kitty keyboard startup fix, Git Bash resolution, browser probe (community contribution) |
| v0.102.0 | Popups word-wrap aware (cursor-anchored); headed Chrome auto-restart on connection loss |

## 7. Miscellaneous

`--dump-requests` debug flag (v0.105.0); `--force` for install (v0.102.0); `cargo binstall` support (v0.100.0); nag system (remind agent about `todo_*` tools after 100 entries, defaults now 200 + disabled, v0.100.0/v0.102.0); hashline implementation removed (v0.108.0); read/write/edit tools aligned to common harness schemas (v0.108.0); Discord lifecycle-script selection (v0.97.0); `@` attachments send even if file missing (highlighted red) and popup scrolls (v0.103.0).

## 8. Trajectory Summary

The project is maturing from a TUI chat client into an **extensible agent harness**: v0.107–v0.110 built the plugin/WASM architecture and pushed citation tracking out of core; MCP grew from new feature to configurable infrastructure; the unreleased subagent system extends the session model into parent/child orchestration. Notably, several core behaviors (citations, themes, personas) now ship as first-party plugins rather than built-ins — consistent with the codebase we explored earlier.

tool_definitions.name: bash
tool_definitions.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. \
            Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB \
            (whichever is hit first). \
            \
            TIMEOUT: the default is 300s. \
            Pass `max_duration_secs` as a tool-call argument to override — NOT the shell `timeout` command. \
            Example: {"command": "cargo test", "max_duration_secs": 600}. \
            Set `max_duration_secs: 0` to disable the timeout for that call.

max_duration_secs.description: Maximum duration in seconds before the command is killed. Overrides the default of 300s. Set to 0 to disable the timeout for this call. Pass as a tool-call argument — NOT the shell `timeout` command. Example: {"command": "cargo test", "max_duration_secs": 600}.

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
prompt_guidelines: Proactively set max_duration_secs for commands that may run long (builds, tests, network requests, large compiles). Do NOT use the shell `timeout` command — pass max_duration_secs as a tool-call argument.
If a command is killed by the timeout, retry the same command with a larger max_duration_secs value.

tool_definitions.name: edit
tool_definitions.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

`old_string` must match existing content exactly, including indentation —
when editing from `read` output, everything after the line-number prefix is
the file content; never include the prefix itself.

The edit fails if `old_string` is not unique in the file: provide a larger
string with more surrounding context, or use `replace_all` to change every
instance (useful for renaming a variable).

Prefer editing existing files; never write new files unless required.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Edit a file by replacing exact text
prompt_guidelines: `old_string` must match the file exactly and be unique; include more surrounding context or use `replace_all` when it is not.
A successful edit returns a numbered snippet of the changed region; use it for nearby follow-up edits without re-reading.
Prefer `edit` over `write` for changes to existing files.

tool_definitions.name: get_time
tool_definitions.description: Returns the current date and time in UTC.

tool_definitions.name: grep
tool_definitions.description: Search files for a pattern using ripgrep (rg). Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

file_type.description: Search only files of the given type (e.g. "rust", "python").

glob.description: Include only files matching the given glob (e.g. "*.rs").

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

tool_definitions.name: read

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Read a file from the local filesystem
prompt_guidelines: Read files before editing them so you can match content exactly.
Batch-read multiple potentially relevant files in a single response.
If `read` is truncated, continue with the `offset` it suggests — do not guess unseen lines.

tool_definitions.name: restart_mcp_server
tool_definitions.description: Restart a dead or broken MCP server so its tools work again. Call this when an `mcp__<server>__*` tool call fails (the server has likely died). Pass the server's name (e.g. `excalimate`) — a full `mcp__<server>__<tool>` tool name is also accepted and silently resolved. This waits until the server has finished restarting (up to 60s for slow-boot servers), then returns whether it is back online. After a successful restart, retry the original tool call. **If this tool reports failure, STOP and wait for user instruction — do not retry.**

server.description: The MCP server to restart, by name (e.g. `excalimate`), or the failing `mcp__<server>__<tool>` tool name (the namespace is stripped).

tool_definitions.name: save_plan
tool_definitions.description: Save a plan file to disk and pin the result so it persists in conversation history through compaction. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

content.description: Content to write to the plan file

path.description: Path to the plan file (relative or absolute)

prompt_guidelines: Use save_plan to write plan files — the result is pinned so the plan stays visible as context shrinks.
Prefer paths under `.plans/<task-slug>/` (e.g. `.plans/my-feature/plan.md`).

tool_definitions.name: session_query
tool_definitions.description:
Query another session's chat history. Use this to inspect conversations in other sessions.

Examples:
  Get the last 5 messages from a session:
    session_query({"session_id": "s-0196a3b2-4f8c-7d2e-8a1b-5c3d2e1f0a0b", "action": "get_recent", "count": 5})

  Search for text in a session:
    session_query({"session_id": "s-0196a3b2-4f8c-7d2e-8a1b-5c3d2e1f0a0b", "action": "search", "query": "hello world"})

action.description: Which query to run: 'get_recent' returns the last N entries, 'search' finds entries matching text.

count.description: For 'get_recent': number of recent entries to return. Defaults to 10.

query.description: For 'search': text to search for in entries.

tool_definitions.name: skill
tool_definitions.description: Load a specific agent skill's content into the conversation context. The skill content is returned in this tool result and pinned in the conversation history for the rest of the conversation. Use this tool when the current task matches a skill's description from the available skills list. Do not call this tool if the skill is already loaded (marked loaded='true' in the available skills list).

name.description: The name of the skill to load (from the available skills list)

tool_definitions.name: task
tool_definitions.description: Delegate a task to a fresh subagent session and block until it finishes. Spawns a new session inheriting your model, cwd, tools, skills, and MCP servers — but with empty history: it sees only the prompt you give it. When its session goes idle, its final chat entry is returned as this tool's result. WHEN TO USE: open-ended search or exploration where the first try may miss; multi-step sub-tasks whose intermediate tool output you don't need; independent sub-tasks in parallel. WHEN NOT TO USE: reading a specific file or symbol (use read/grep directly); one obvious tool call; tasks that depend on each other's results. Usage notes: (1) The prompt must be self-contained — the subagent cannot see this conversation or the user's intent; say whether it should research or make changes. (2) Launch independent tasks concurrently — multiple task calls in one message. (3) The user can watch and steer the subagent live; cancelling it returns the cancel to you as the result. (4) Only the final message comes back; intermediate work stays in the subagent's session. TIMEOUT: unlimited by default. Pass `max_duration_secs` to bound the subagent; on expiry the subagent is cancelled and a failure is returned.

description.description: A 3-5 word summary of the task, shown as the subagent session's title in the sidebar.

max_duration_secs.description: Maximum duration in seconds to wait for the subagent. Unlimited by default; 0 also means unlimited. On expiry the subagent session is cancelled and a failure is returned.

model.description: Optional model id for the subagent. Defaults to this session's model.

prompt.description: Self-contained brief for the subagent. It sees nothing else — no conversation history, no user intent.

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Spawn a subagent session for a self-contained sub-task and await its result
prompt_guidelines: Prefer task for open-ended exploration; keep focused lookups (read/grep) in your own context.
Write the prompt as a complete brief: goal, constraints, and whether to research or make changes. Include a description so the user can follow along in the sidebar.

tool_definitions.name: todo_add_phase
tool_definitions.description: Add a new phase (task group) to the todo list. Phases are high-level stages of work. Each phase can contain multiple tasks. Returns the new phase ID and the updated todo list.
tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Add a new phase to the task list to organize work into stages
prompt_guidelines: Use todo_add_phase to define high-level stages before adding individual tasks.
Phase descriptions should be short and descriptive (e.g., 'Research', 'Build', 'Test').

tool_definitions.name: todo_add_task
tool_definitions.description: Add a new task to a phase in the todo list. Optionally position it relative to another task using after_task or before_task. When neither is specified, the task is appended to the end of the phase. Returns the new task ID and the updated todo list.

after_task.description: Optional: insert after this task ID (e.g., 't3'). Mutually exclusive with before_task.

before_task.description: Optional: insert before this task ID (e.g., 't3'). Mutually exclusive with after_task.

phase_id.description: ID of the phase to add the task to (e.g., 'p1')

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Add a task to a phase in the task list
prompt_guidelines: Specify after_task to insert after a specific task, or before_task to insert before one.
Do not specify both after_task and before_task - they are mutually exclusive.
When neither is specified, the task is appended to the end of the phase.

tool_definitions.name: todo_cancel_task
tool_definitions.description: Cancel a task — mark it as not happening. Cancelled tasks remain visible to the agent with a CANCELLED: prefix to prevent re-implementation of abandoned work.

task_id.description: ID of the task to cancel (e.g., 't3')

prompt_guidelines: Cancelled tasks are hidden from the sidebar but remain visible in the task list with a CANCELLED: prefix.
Use cancel when a task is not happening at all — not just postponed.

tool_definitions.name: todo_complete_task
tool_definitions.description: Mark a task in the todo list as completed.

task_id.description: ID of the task to mark as completed (e.g., 't3')

tool_definitions.name: todo_get_phase
tool_definitions.description: Get a single phase with its tasks from the todo list. Returns the phase description and all tasks in that phase.

phase_id.description: ID of the phase to retrieve (e.g., 'p1')

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Get details for a specific phase

tool_definitions.name: todo_get_task_list
tool_definitions.description: Get the full todo list with all phases and tasks. Returns the current state of the todo list for review.

tool_definitions.name: todo_postpone_task
tool_definitions.description: Postpone a task by marking it as postponed (▼) and creating a pending copy at a new location. The source task remains in place but is excluded from agent-facing task list output. The new copy is placed relative to a reference task, which determines the target phase.

after_task.description: Create the new copy after this task. Mutually exclusive with before_task.

before_task.description: Create the new copy before this task. Mutually exclusive with after_task.

task_id.description: ID of the task to postpone

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Postpone a task to a different location
prompt_guidelines: Exactly one of after_task or before_task is required to position the postponed copy.
The source task is marked as postponed (▼) and will not appear in agent-facing task list queries.
Use todo_add_phase first if you need to postpone into a new phase.

tool_definitions.name: todo_postpone_to_phase
tool_definitions.description: Postpone a task by marking it as postponed (▼) and creating a pending copy at the end of a target phase. Using target_phase_id moves the task to an existing phase. Using phase_description creates a new phase and moves the task there. These two options are mutually exclusive. The source task remains in place but is excluded from agent-facing task list output.

phase_description.description: Description for a new phase to create and postpone the task into. Mutually exclusive with target_phase_id.

target_phase_id.description: ID of an existing phase to postpone the task to. Mutually exclusive with phase_description.

task_id.description: ID of the task to postpone

tool_definitions.prompt_snippet: Postpone a task to a phase
prompt_guidelines: Use target_phase_id to postpone to an existing phase. Use phase_description to create a new phase and postpone into it. These are mutually exclusive.
The copy is always appended to the end of the target phase. Use todo_postpone_task if you need to position the copy relative to a specific task.
The source task is marked as postponed (▼) and will not appear in agent-facing task list queries.

tool_definitions.name: todo_set_list
tool_definitions.description: Replace the entire task list with a new one. Accepts an ordered list of phases, each containing an ordered list of task descriptions. All existing phases and tasks are discarded. All new tasks are created with Pending status. Use this when you have a complete plan ready to materialize.

phases.description: Ordered list of phases. Each phase has a description and an optional list of task descriptions.

tasks.description: Ordered list of task descriptions for this phase.

prompt_guidelines: Provide the full plan - all phases and tasks - in a single call. Existing phases and tasks are replaced entirely.
Each phase must have a description. Tasks within a phase are optional.
To preserve existing phases, read the current list first and include them.

tool_definitions.name: write
tool_definitions.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting the existing file 
            if one exists at the provided path. Parent directories are created automatically.


            Prefer editing existing files; never create new files unless required, and never 
            create documentation files (*.md, README) unless the user explicitly asks.

content.description: The content to write to the file

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

prompt_guidelines: Only use `write` for new files or complete rewrites — use `edit` for changes.

tool_definitions.name: mcp__parallel-search__web_fetch
tool_definitions.description:
Purpose: Fetch and extract relevant content
from specific web URLs. Use only when web_search excerpts are insufficient
for the task at hand.

Ideal Use Cases:
- The user asked about a specific URL or page
- You need exact wording or quotes that excerpts may have truncated
- You need full-page analysis (long article, document, or page structure)
- web_search excerpts are conflicting or clearly insufficient to answer

full_content.description:
Prefer leaving this off. The default
excerpt mode returns LLM-optimized snippets focused on your objective — they
are much smaller, cheaper, and usually all you need. Only set to true when
you explicitly need the entire page as markdown (e.g. reading a long article
in full, or running a document through a downstream summarizer).

Warning: enabling full content can return a large amount of content —
often tens of thousands of tokens for a long article. This may exceed your
MCP client's tool-output limit and will substantially increase response
size and latency.
full_content.title: Full Content

model_name.description: The identifier of the LLM model making this tool call (e.g. 'claude-opus-4.7', 'gpt-5.5', 'gemini-2.5-pro'). Before the first call, verify the exact active model slug from trusted runtime/session metadata or active client configuration. Pass the full slug verbatim; never shorten or substitute a model-family alias like 'gpt-5'. Used for product analytics only; does not affect search behavior.

objective.description:
Natural-language description of what
information you're looking for from the URLs. Limit to 200 characters.
objective.title: Objective

search_queries.description:
Optional keyword search queries (3-6
words each) used together with objective to focus excerpts on the most
relevant content. Pass the queries from the prior web_search call that
surfaced these URLs, if applicable.
search_queries.title: Search Queries

session_id.description: Stable identifier for the current conversation. Generate a random value (UUID or 32+ character hex string) at the start of your session and reuse the exact same value on every web_search / web_fetch call. Do NOT change it between turns. Used for free-tier rate limiting and correlating your tool calls in our logs; ignored on paid-tier keys.

urls.description:
List of URLs to extract content from. Must be
valid HTTP/HTTPS URLs. Up to 20 URLs per request.
urls.title: Urls

tool_definitions.name: mcp__parallel-search__web_search
tool_definitions.description:
Purpose: Perform web searches and return
LLM-friendly results, including excerpts that are usually sufficient to
answer directly without a follow-up fetch.

Ideal Use Cases:
- Answering questions that require fresh or current information
- Research, comparison, documentation, and troubleshooting questions
- Broad tasks where multiple `search_queries` can be issued in a single call

model_name.description: The identifier of the LLM model making this tool call (e.g. 'claude-opus-4.7', 'gpt-5.5', 'gemini-2.5-pro'). Before the first call, verify the exact active model slug from trusted runtime/session metadata or active client configuration. Pass the full slug verbatim; never shorten or substitute a model-family alias like 'gpt-5'. Used for product analytics only; does not affect search behavior.

objective.description:
Natural-language description of what the web search is trying to find.
Try to make the search objective atomic, looking for a specific piece of information. May include guidance about preferred sources or freshness.
objective.title: Objective

search_queries.description:
Concise keyword search queries, 3-6 words
each, which may include search operators. At least one query is required;
provide 2-3 for best results. For broad tasks, you can include multiple
related queries in a single call instead of chaining web_search calls. The
queries should be related to the objective.
search_queries.title: Search Queries

session_id.description: Stable identifier for the current conversation. Generate a random value (UUID or 32+ character hex string) at the start of your session and reuse the exact same value on every web_search / web_fetch call. Do NOT change it between turns. Used for free-tier rate limiting and correlating your tool calls in our logs; ignored on paid-tier keys.
